p01.why: The dependent base Base<T> is not searched, so count is the global count with value 5.

p02.why: sizeof of the function type void(T) is valid only for an empty pack; no diagnostic is required and every compiler accepts, and count() returns 0.

p03.why: A fold expression is type-dependent, so argument-dependent lookup at the instantiation finds shop::price.

p04.why: Both::m finds Fixed::m at the definition and Extra::m at the instantiation; no diagnostic is required and every compiler accepts and uses the second member.

p05.why: Box has a dependent base, so Box::make is looked up at the instantiation and finds Base<int>::make.

p06.why: typename T::type finds a static data member, which is not a type.

p07.why: Box::missing is looked up at the instantiation, also in the dependent base.

p08.why: Both::f finds Fixed::f at the definition and Extra::f at the instantiation; every compiler accepts and uses the second member.

p09.why: probe has dependent explicit template arguments, so argument-dependent lookup at the instantiation finds lib::probe.

p10.why: The base Outer<T> is the current instantiation of the enclosing class, so it is searched and value() is Outer::value.

p11.why: The better probe(Item, int) is only in the other unit; no diagnostic is required, the call uses probe(Item, double), and the program checks for either result.

p12.why: helper(1) has no dependent argument, so helper must be declared before the template.

p13.why: Argument-dependent lookup at the instantiation finds the better probe(Item, int).

p14.why: The template body has a syntax error.

p15.why: item is a member alias of the current instantiation with an independent target, so the call is bound at the definition to pick(Item, long).

p16.why: The template keyword is used in every dependent position and is allowed before independent names, so the sum is 9 and plain gives 3.

p17.why: f finds Fixed::f in the independent base at the definition and keeps it, so the static_assert holds.

p18.why: The other unit's probe(Item, unsigned) would make the call ambiguous; no diagnostic is required and no compiler or linker reports it, so probe(Item, long) gives 1.

p19.why: size is declared only in the dependent base and is used as a type without qualification.

p20.why: sizeof(T::type) without typename is accepted by EDG and rejected by Clang and GCC (Q-0224).

p21.why: A block variable declaration is not a type-only position, so T::type is read as a value.

p22.why: The alias target, named cast, default type argument, constant parameter type, and lambda parameter are type-only positions.

p23.why: The discarded branch has no valid specialization; no diagnostic is required, and the branch is not instantiated for int.

p24.why: this->count, Derived::count, and Base<T>::count all reach the dependent base member, so the sum is 3.

p25.why: sizeof and a cast to int are not type-dependent, so both calls bind at the definition to probe(Tag, double).

p26.why: T::box as a template template argument needs the template keyword.

p27.why: make has a deduced return type in the current instantiation, so make() is type-dependent and lookup at the instantiation finds price.

p28.why: Every construct depends on T and some argument list makes it valid.

p29.why: A function template parameter is not a type-only position, so T::type needs typename.

p30.why: sizeof... and the fold are value-dependent bounds, giving 3 elements each.

p31.why: using typename Base<T>::size_type declares a type name in the class.

p32.why: Inner and Outer<T>::Inner name the current instantiation, so their member types need no typename.

p33.why: Argument-dependent lookup at the instantiation finds lib::probe declared after the template.

p34.why: The noexcept condition is value-dependent, so p has a dependent type and argument-dependent lookup finds shop::price.

p35.why: Base::N in the independent base hides the parameter, inside the class and in the outside definition.

p36.why: Box<T*> is another specialization, so Box<T*>::type needs typename.

p37.why: Every use of T::type is in a type-only position, and the values add up to 35.

p38.why: Clang finds the conversion function operator T of the dependent base without this-> and returns 0; GCC and EDG do not and reject (Q-0248).

p39.why: T::template box with no argument list is valid as the default of a template template parameter.

p40.why: object is type-dependent, so get<int> after -> needs the template keyword.

p41.why: sizeof... is never type-dependent, so the call binds at the definition to probe(Tag, double).

p42.why: Later is independent and is declared after the template.

p43.why: A unary operator with Item as its first parameter leaves no room for the pack.

p44.why: Base::U hides the parameter U inside the class and in the outside definition, so both checks see int.

p45.why: m finds Fixed::m at the definition and keeps it, so Extra::m does not make it ambiguous.

p46.why: helper is an undeclared independent name, and every compiler rejects it also in an unused template.

p47.why: At the instantiation with int, T::count is not valid.

p48.why: All the dependent types and names are checked at the instantiation with Item, where they are valid.

p49.why: pick(1) is independent and binds to pick(double) at the definition.

p50.why: typename T::box<int> without template is accepted by GCC and rejected by Clang and EDG (Q-0225).

p51.why: operator+ is declared after the template in the global namespace, which is not associated with shop::Item.

p52.why: T(0) is a cast to a dependent type, so the call is dependent and finds probe(Tag, int) at the instantiation.

p53.why: Box has no dependent base, so Box::missing must be found, and the class is instantiated.

p54.why: An invalid independent conversion in an unused template: Clang and EDG reject, GCC accepts (Q-0223).

p55.why: Without typename the using-declaration does not declare a type name, so type cannot declare value.

p56.why: The independent base Base is searched, so count is Base::count.

p57.why: The argument is int, which adds no namespace, so probe declared later is not found.

p58.why: typename T::type finds nothing in Has.

p59.why: shop::Tag<N> and shop::List<T...> are dependent types, so argument-dependent lookup finds both price templates.

p60.why: T::make<int> needs the template keyword after a dependent qualifier.

p61.why: T::box<int> as a base without template is accepted by GCC and rejected by Clang and EDG (Q-0225).

p62.why: The qualified call finds probe at the definition and a later declaration adds a default; GCC uses the default and returns 0, Clang and EDG reject (Q-0249).

p63.why: N - 1 is a value-dependent bound, 4 for N = 5.

p64.why: For N = 1 the array has bound 0, which is not valid.

p65.why: count is declared only in the dependent base, and every compiler rejects such a name also in an unused template.

p66.why: Box, Box<T>, and ::Box<T> name the current instantiation, so type needs no typename.

p67.why: copy is an auto variable with a type-dependent initializer, so the call is dependent and finds shop::price.

p68.why: this->m is ambiguous between Fixed::m and Extra::m at the instantiation.

p69.why: The unqualified dependent call finds the redeclaration with the default argument at the instantiation, so it returns 4.

p70.why: T::count is read as a value, so n is a variable with the value 2 and the result is 12.

p71.why: A braced list with a type-dependent element makes the call dependent, so helper is looked up only at an instantiation.

p72.why: count is declared only in the dependent base.

p73.why: In the partial specialization, Box<T*> and Box name the current instantiation.

p74.why: An alias for the type parameter counts as that parameter, so Box<self> is the current instantiation.

p75.why: template after the qualifier of a declared name: GCC and EDG accept, Clang rejects (Q-0227).

p76.why: V has a placeholder type, so price(V) is dependent and argument-dependent lookup finds shop::price.

p77.why: typename T::template box with deduced arguments: GCC and EDG accept, Clang rejects (Q-0226).

p78.why: typename T::type is looked up again for each specialization.

p79.why: A template argument is not a type-only position, so T::type needs typename.

p80.why: A function type with a parameter pack is dependent, so argument-dependent lookup finds shop::price.

p81.why: T::value is looked up for each specialization.

p82.why: A pack expansion argument makes the call dependent.

p83.why: Box::missing finds nothing in a class with no dependent base; the template is unused, so GCC 14 accepts and the other compilers reject (Q-0228).

p84.why: T::count is read as a value, but Has::count is a type.

p85.why: count is a const int initialized from N, so it is a value-dependent constant bound.

p86.why: The template keyword before a destructor name; Clang and GCC reject, EDG accepts (Q-0245). The record names the arrow form, and I assume the dot form behaves the same.

p87.why: A base list that expands one pack twice: Clang and EDG reject, GCC accepts until the class is instantiated (Q-0247).

p88.why: typename does not change lookup, and lookup of name finds the data member.

p89.why: probe is declared after the template in the global namespace, which is not associated with lib::Item.

p90.why: The name after typename must be a qualified name.

p91.why: In the partial specialization Box<T> is another specialization, so Box<T>::type needs typename.

p92.why: template after the qualifier of a declared name: GCC and EDG accept, Clang rejects (Q-0227).

p93.why: Box<M> with a static constant member M names another specialization, so Box<M>::type needs typename.

p94.why: a + b has type-dependent operands, so argument-dependent lookup finds shop::operator+.

p95.why: Both::m becomes ambiguous at the instantiation: Clang and EDG reject, GCC keeps Fixed::m (Q-0230).

p96.why: Every compiler rejects T::box<int> without template as an alias target.

p97.why: The constexpr variable needs limit, defined after the template: Clang rejects, GCC and EDG accept and return 0 (Q-0250).

p98.why: No argument list makes the template valid; no diagnostic is required and every compiler accepts.

p99.why: The template is never instantiated, so whether plain is a template is not checked.

p100.why: An invalid independent call in an unused template: Clang and EDG reject, GCC accepts (Q-0223).

p101.why: object.template field for a data member: GCC accepts, Clang and EDG reject (Q-0226).

p102.why: using typename declares type as a type name.

p103.why: typename can come before an independent qualified name, inside or outside a template.

p104.why: Same<T> is an alias that gives Box<T>; Clang and GCC treat it as the current instantiation and accept, EDG rejects (Q-0229).

p105.why: p->template ~T(): Clang and GCC reject, EDG accepts (Q-0245).

p106.why: sizeof of a class that is incomplete at the definition is rejected by every compiler.

p107.why: plain is not a template, so T::template plain<int> is not valid at the instantiation.

p108.why: sizeof(int(T)) is valid only for an empty pack; no diagnostic is required and the empty case gives 0.
